subject: Cortado-4b onboarding exception & ingestion checklist
body:
From: Sam Brown <sam.brown@datasolve.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Cortado-4b onboarding exception + ingest

Hi Stephanie / Marcus,

Thanks for taking a look — quick background: DataSolve is planning to ship an assistant powered by Cortado-4b (variant: cortado-4b-adapter-v2) and we hit a blocker on your onboarding checklist. The model uses a non-standard byte-pair tokenization and a small, custom KV cache layout that means the default ingestion path flags it as incompatible. Our security/compliance docs are in the attached compat_report_Cortado-4b.pdf.

What we need from Redwood:
- A temporary onboarding exception to ingest the variant into a staging project (we can keep it private).
- Guidance on whether we should pin to cortado-4b-adapter-v2 or ingest both v2 and v2-legacy; we expect rapid iteration so a flexible pin policy would help.
- An agreed mutual action plan (MAM) and timeline — target is a staged canary next week if possible (tight).

We can provide telemetry hooks and limited sample traffic for canary. Also copying our legal contact in case there are contract/NDAs needed.

Attachments: compat_report_Cortado-4b.pdf (5 pages — tokenizer notes, mem footprint, SOC references)

Best,
Sam Brown
Product Lead, Integrations
DataSolve
sam.brown@datasolve.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Brown <sam.brown@datasolve.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Cortado-4b onboarding exception + ingest

Thanks Sam — appreciate the packet. I skimmed the compat report and want to align cross-functionally before we commit to a timeline. High level asks from our side:

- Product: clear definition of the acceptance criteria for canary (latency SLO, failure rate, prompt set).
- Infra/Runtime: exact sequence lengths and KV-cache expectations; confirm whether the adapter writes nonstandard KV headers.
- Security/Legal: any PII processing expectations and whether the variant will be used in Private deployment or Hosted.

Proposed next steps (quick):
1) Marcus to validate runtime kernel/path compatibility and provide a short list of required changes or mitigations.
2) Lauren (product ops) to draft a MAM with checkpoints (staging ingress, canary traffic, rollback criteria).
3) Stephanie to request a temporary pin exception for that variant (30 days) so it can be exercised in a private staging project.

If we can agree on the acceptance criteria by EOD Wednesday (PST) we can target a Thursday canary. Marcus — reassigning to you for a quick compatibility assessment; I put the key items below so we have a single checklist.

Checklist (what I need back from infra before we say yes):
- Kernel/op compatibility: conv/attention path OK? any fallback kernels required?
- Memory/throughput delta estimate at 1k RPS and at 50 concurrent sessions.
- Telemetry hooks we need instrumented (per-request model_id, token-level timing, OOM alarms).
- Suggested pin policy: pin to v2 OR allow staged dual-serve (hosted fallback to v1).

Thanks — Steph

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Sam Brown <sam.brown@datasolve.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Cortado-4b onboarding exception + ingest

Hey team, quick tech readout after looking through the compat PDF and a few local tests. TL;DR: doable with limited infra changes, we should scope an exception with tight rollback criteria.

Notes:
- Tokenizer mismatch: runtime can support custom tokenizers but we must persist an adapter mapping on ingest. That adapter adds ~1.8ms/token overhead in the worst case; for short chats it's negligible but at scale will matter.
- KV layout: the custom KV header means our current KV-cache layer needs a small compatibility shim; I estimate ~2 engineer-days to implement and test a shim that normalizes headers into our canonical KV format.
- Memory: peak working set +15% on the same sequence batch sizes. On our staging 16GB-GPU pool we saw an extra 2.1GB at 512-seq. If DataSolve will run sustained long context sessions we should prioritize a quantized kernel path.
- Kernel selection: no fundamental kernel rewriting required; some kernel scheduling heuristics need a param tweak for the adapter to avoid tail latency spikes.

Suggested immediate plan:
1) Grant a 14-day pin exception for cortado-4b-adapter-v2 into a private staging project with strict tagging and access control.
2) Implement KV shim in a short branch; run a 48-hour soak with limited synthetic traffic (we can provide a harness).
3) Instrument telemetry: model_variant, token_latency_ms, kv_miss_rate, oom_alert.
4) Post-canary rollback criteria: >2% increase in 99th latency OR >3 OOMs in 24 hours triggers automatic rollback.

I'll attach a quick notes file (kernel-diff-notes.txt) with command lines and perf snippets. If Product is OK, I can start the shim work tomorrow and aim for a Thursday canary.

—Marcus

Hi Stephanie / Marcus,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear checklist. We can comply with the instrumentations and will send the required sample prompt sets + telemetry hooks by tomorrow morning. We are comfortable with a 14-day exception (works for our release cadence) — legal included and ready to sign the narrow NDA for the staging project.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed: final acceptance criteria and signed NDA
- Thu: start shim + small ingest into private staging (sanity traffic)
- Thu afternoon: limited canary (10k tokens total)
- Fri: soak + metrics review; decision to widen traffic on Mon

We will also provide a small dataset of long-context sessions to validate memory and tail latency. Let us know if you want that earlier.

Appreciate the collaboration — Sam

Product Lead, Integrations
